card.name: Sentence-ending periods in drug label text
card.fires_on: The period (or comma) that closes a sentence or clause in drug-label prose, often right after a list of drugs, doses or conditions. The next text starts a new section or sentence.

modes.label: Period after a drug list
modes.description: A full stop closing a list of drug names or classes, just before a new heading or sentence.
modes.example: ine, amitriptyline, nortriptyline), valproate, warfarin, ziprasidone, zonisamide<<.>> Other Drug Interactions Cyclophosph

modes.label: Period after dosing statement
modes.description: A full stop ending a sentence about dose, administration or preparation, before a new section.
modes.example: of this solution corresponding to a 10 mg/kg dose may be administered orally via an oral dosing syringe<<.>> Table 1 provides dosing information for

modes.label: Comma ending a clause in a list of factors
modes.description: A comma after an item in a series of factors, with more items following.
modes.example: the depth of anesthesia and degree of muscle relaxation required<<,>> the duration of anesthesia desired, individual tolerance
